signals.evidence: NotificationService::send_to_user's NotificationChannel::Push branch (services/notification.rs:348-356) only calls tracing::info! with an 'integration pending' comment and never dispatches to FCM/APNs — yet every scheduler-triggered notifier (notify_announcement_published L453-457, notify_vote_started L488-492, notify_vote_closed, notify_meter_reading_due, notify_payment_due) lists NotificationChannel::Push and the scheduler invokes them (scheduler/mod.rs:491, :986, :1066, :1152; scheduler/votes.rs:96, :256, :486), so all scheduled-announcement / vote-lifecycle / meter / payment push notifications silently drop in production while the request-time path (routes/announcements/lifecycle.rs:138, routes/voting.rs:739, etc.) correctly uses state.notification_pipeline which fans out to the PushFanoutWorker.
signals.title: Scheduler push notifications silently dropped by NotificationService stub
signals.suggested_fix_sketch: Replace the NotificationService usage in Scheduler with the already-wired state.notification_pipeline (NotificationPipeline::broadcast / dispatch_to_users), which routes NotificationChannel::Push through CombinedPushAdapter and the PushFanoutWorker — matching how the request-time paths already dispatch.
signals.severity_upgrade_note: reviewer called it medium (+2); routine upgraded to high (+3) because it is a silent-failure correctness bug affecting ALL scheduled push paths (announcements, votes, meters, payments), not a perf/UX smell

signals.evidence: FeatureService::resolve_features_for_user (services/feature_service.rs:73-166) loops over every flag returned by flag_repo.list_all() and inside the loop issues per-flag DB round trips: analytics_repo.get_user_type_access (L95-98, single-row SELECT from user_type_feature_access), analytics_repo.get_descriptor (L101, single-row SELECT from feature_descriptors), plus resolve_feature_state (L170-218) which calls flag_repo.is_enabled_for_context then has_specific_override (L221-285) running 2-3 additional EXISTS queries against feature_flag_overrides per flag — so each flag costs 3-6 queries and the authenticated hot path GET /api/v1/features/resolved (routes/features.rs:242-273) scales as O(flags) × 3-6 instead of a constant number of batched joins.
signals.title: O(flags) DB round trips in FeatureService::resolve_features_for_user
signals.suggested_fix_sketch: Replace the per-flag lookups with batched fetches at the top of the function: one SELECT returning all user_type_feature_access rows for the user_type, one for all feature_descriptors, and a single SELECT from feature_flag_overrides filtered by (user_id, org_id, role_id) grouped by flag_id — then resolve from in-memory maps.
